title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
statement: Remove the nth node from the end of the list and return the remaining values. `n` is always valid.
hints: Two passes work: count the length, then delete length - n.
One pass uses a gap of n nodes between a fast pointer and a slow pointer.
A dummy head makes deleting the first node the same as deleting any other node.

approaches.name: Fast and slow gap
approaches.explanation: When fast falls off, slow stands before the target.

editorial: Advance fast n + 1 steps from the dummy, so the gap includes the dummy. Then move both pointers until fast is null. Slow.next is the node to delete. Splice it out with slow.next = slow.next.next.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def remove_nth_from_end(head: list[int], n: int) -> list[int]:
    dummy = _node_chain([0])
    dummy.nxt = _node_chain(head)
    fast = slow = dummy
    for _ in range(n + 1):
        fast = fast.nxt
    while fast is not None:
        fast = fast.nxt
        slow = slow.nxt
    slow.nxt = slow.nxt.nxt
    return _to_list(dummy.nxt)
